lessons.title: Series, DataFrames and labeled data
lessons.motivation: Labels carry identity that positional matrices alone do not.
lessons.progression: Reorder Series labels, then remove one label to expose alignment/missingness.
lessons.terms: Series, DataFrame, index, column, dtype, nullable value, schema.
lessons.math: Observation/feature matrices plus explicit labels and row identity.
lessons.worked: a=pd.Series([1,2],index=['rowA','rowB']) and b=pd.Series([10,20],index=['rowB','rowA']); a+b yields rowA:21,rowB:12 by labels, not position.
lessons.misconception: A DataFrame is not simply a NumPy matrix with decorative labels.

objectives.outcome: Predict label alignment and preserve row identity.
objectives.assessment: Diagnose an incorrect position-based Series sum and explain matching labels.
objectives.remediation: Draw index-to-value mappings before adding.

objectives.outcome: Read shape, columns, index and dtypes from a small table.
objectives.assessment: Select a valid feature schema after inspection.
objectives.remediation: Use the metadata panel, not visual row numbers.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish a Series selection from a one-column DataFrame.
objectives.assessment: Predict dimensions after single versus list-of-column selection.
objectives.remediation: Compare df['area'] with df[['area']].

objectives.outcome: Identify nullable numeric/string data without inventing zeros.
objectives.assessment: Choose field types and missing-value markers for a new table.
objectives.remediation: Review explicit schema/nullability definitions.

lessons.title: Selecting and filtering without losing alignment
lessons.motivation: Selection is a cohort and feature-contract decision, not just bracket syntax.
lessons.progression: Contrast label/position lookup, then a reordered Boolean mask.
lessons.terms: loc, iloc, Boolean Series, index label, positional selection, explicit assignment.
lessons.math: A filter is a selection function; masks have identity as well as length.
lessons.worked: With row labels [10,20,30], df.loc[20] selects label 20; df.iloc[1] selects the second row. These coincide here, not by definition.
lessons.misconception: .loc[0] need not mean the first row; a filter can be valid Python but wrong for the intended cohort.

objectives.outcome: Predict .loc and .iloc values with nontrivial indexes.
objectives.assessment: Select the exact resulting rows from a changed index.
objectives.remediation: Label positions separately from index values.

objectives.outcome: Apply the intended filter to aligned observations/targets.
objectives.assessment: Repair a misaligned or inappropriate cohort mask and justify retained IDs.
objectives.remediation: Compare the mask index with the table index.

objectives.outcome: Select columns without silently changing feature order.
objectives.assessment: Choose the ordered model input columns.
objectives.remediation: Match the downstream coefficient names.

objectives.outcome: Use explicit .loc assignment or .copy() under the pinned pandas behavior.
objectives.assessment: Choose a repair without relying on chained assignment side effects.
objectives.remediation: Trace the deliberately owned frame and resulting values.

lessons.title: Missing values require a stated policy
lessons.motivation: A missingness policy changes data and assumptions, not only cell appearance.
lessons.progression: Keep legitimate zero, compare drop/fill, then distinguish exploratory versus training use.
lessons.terms: isna, notna, fillna, dropna, nullable dtype, missingness rate.
lessons.math: Denominators and summaries change when observations are removed.
lessons.worked: Ages [0, missing,20] have one missing value, not two. Filling with observed median 10 gives [0,10,20]; this exploratory example is not permission to fit on test data.
lessons.misconception: Empty-looking values, zeros and missing labels are not equivalent; imputation is an assumption.

objectives.outcome: Detect missingness without discarding valid zero values.
objectives.assessment: Repair a truthiness-based missingness rule and explain zero retention.
objectives.remediation: Use isna masks beside original values.

objectives.outcome: Compute missingness counts/rates with the correct denominator.
objectives.assessment: Select the count and fraction for a changed column.
objectives.remediation: Count all eligible rows before dividing.

objectives.outcome: Predict fillna/dropna effects on values and shape.
objectives.assessment: Choose the resulting table after a stated policy.
objectives.remediation: Compare retained row IDs and replacement values.

objectives.outcome: Separate exploratory filling from training-fitted preprocessing.
objectives.assessment: Reject whole-dataset median fitting before a split.
objectives.remediation: Revisit the earlier Statistics leakage lesson and the local fit-boundary explanation; T02 is an optional later extension, not a prerequisite.

lessons.title: Grouping, aggregating and reporting denominators
lessons.motivation: Grouped summaries have group-specific denominators and cannot be averaged blindly.
lessons.progression: Rebuild group sums/counts, then include missing keys and unequal sizes.
lessons.terms: groupby, agg, count, size, group key, missing group, sort.
lessons.math: Group means, weighted totals and conditional summaries.
lessons.worked: Groups A:[10,20], B:[100] have means 15 and 100. Their unweighted mean 57.5 is not the overall mean 130/3.
lessons.misconception: A mean of group means need not equal the global mean; count excludes missing values while size counts rows.

objectives.outcome: Predict an explicitly configured groupby aggregation.
objectives.assessment: Select grouped sum/mean values for a changed table.
objectives.remediation: List membership before calculating.

objectives.outcome: Use correct group denominators and distinguish size from count.
objectives.assessment: Reject a mean-of-means or missing-count error and explain the denominator.
objectives.remediation: Reconstruct sum and count for each group.

objectives.outcome: Handle missing keys and category inclusion explicitly.
objectives.assessment: Choose the result under stated dropna/observed settings.
objectives.remediation: Compare groups included versus excluded by the policy.

objectives.outcome: Avoid causal conclusions from group differences.
objectives.assessment: Identify a confounding-compatible interpretation.
objectives.remediation: Return to the Statistics observational/intervention experiment.

lessons.title: Joins can duplicate or lose observations
lessons.motivation: Joining constructs matching pairs and can change effective observation weights.
lessons.progression: Count duplicate matches, then apply a cardinality contract and unmatched/null-key policy.
lessons.terms: merge, join key, inner, left, cardinality, validate, indicator, duplicate.
lessons.math: Relational matching changes sample weights and row multiplicities.
lessons.worked: Left keys [A,B] and right keys [A,A] produce three rows in a left join (two A matches and one unmatched B); an inner join produces two.
lessons.misconception: Joining does not guarantee one row per customer; equal column names do not prove a valid key.

objectives.outcome: Choose valid join keys and an explicit matching contract.
objectives.assessment: Diagnose an inappropriate key and justify a stable entity ID.
objectives.remediation: Inspect uniqueness, meaning and missing keys.

objectives.outcome: Predict duplication/loss and reject unexpected many-to-many joins.
objectives.assessment: Choose row count/matches and a validate repair.
objectives.remediation: Draw the matching pairs, then count multiplicities.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish inner from left join and inspect unmatched rows.
objectives.assessment: Select retained IDs plus an indicator result.
objectives.remediation: Compare the requested population before/after joining.

objectives.outcome: Recognize that pandas null-key matching needs explicit handling.
objectives.assessment: Reject an assumed SQL-style nonmatch for null keys.
objectives.remediation: Inspect the pinned merge null-key fixture.

lessons.title: A reproducible dataset audit
lessons.motivation: An audit asks whether rows/features are usable for a stated prediction-time question.
lessons.progression: Inspect a derived faulty table, then produce a justified audit record.
lessons.terms: read_csv, schema, duplicate row, parse date, provenance, target, audit report.
lessons.math: Summary statistics are meaningful only for the stated rows, units and split.
lessons.worked: A 16-row fictional housing table contains a duplicate ID, a missing age and a target-like future_price column. A useful audit reports these rather than blindly calling describe().
lessons.misconception: A dataframe that loads successfully is not automatically suitable model input.

objectives.outcome: Inspect bundled CSV types, dates and missing markers deterministically.
objectives.assessment: Select an explicit loader/parse rule and schema mismatch.
objectives.remediation: Compare raw strings with the declared schema.

objectives.outcome: Report duplicates/missingness/group counts using row identities.
objectives.assessment: Choose a reproducible small-table audit summary.
objectives.remediation: Revisit D03–D05 counts and key checks.

objectives.outcome: Exclude targets and unavailable-at-prediction columns from features.
objectives.assessment: Identify target/future leakage and justify the timing boundary.
objectives.remediation: Build the feature-availability timeline.

objectives.outcome: Produce a bounded audit record with provenance and limitations.
objectives.assessment: Select the complete report fields rather than an unsupported population claim.
objectives.remediation: Use the dataset manifest and exact retained IDs.
